players.product: wafer-level burn-in systems (FOX) with WaferPak full-wafer contactors, and Sonoma package-level burn-in, for AI accelerators and silicon photonics

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Chris Siu: second quarter revenue was $9.9 million, down 27% from $13.5 million in the prior-year period, primarily on lower WaferPak shipments, partially offset by stronger demand for Sonoma systems from the hyperscaler customer. Contactor revenue (WaferPaks for wafer-level burn-in plus BIMs and BIBs for packaged-part burn-in) totaled $3.4 million, 35% of total revenue, vs $8.6 million or 64% a year earlier; non-GAAP gross margin was 29.8% vs 45.3% on lower volume and less high-margin WaferPak mix; non-GAAP net loss was $1.3 million, or negative $0.04 per diluted share. The CEO said second quarter revenue was softer than anticipated.
quarterly_data.figure: $9.9 million revenue (down 27% from $13.5 million); contactors $3.4 million (35%); non-GAAP gross margin 29.8% vs 45.3%; non-GAAP net loss $1.3 million

quarterly_data.signal: Bookings and backlog: Q2 bookings were $6.2 million vs $11.4 million in Q1, and quarter-end backlog was $11.8 million. In the first 6 weeks of Q3 Aehr booked an additional $6.5 million, driven primarily by an order from a premier Silicon Valley test lab (not named) for the newly introduced high-power configured Sonoma system, lifting effective backlog to $18.3 million.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 bookings $6.2 million (vs $11.4 million in Q1); backlog $11.8 million; $6.5 million booked early in Q3; effective backlog $18.3 million

quarterly_data.signal: Aehr reinstated guidance: for the second half of fiscal '26 (November 29, 2025 to May 29, 2026) it expects revenue between $25 million and $30 million and non-GAAP net loss per diluted share between negative $0.09 and negative $0.05. It gives no formal bookings guidance, but based on recent customer forecasts management believes second-half bookings will be 'much higher than revenue', between $60 million and $80 million, setting up 'a very strong fiscal '27' that begins May 30, 2026. In Q&A the CEO said the bulk is wafer-level and packaged-part burn-in for AI processors (packaged-part AI the biggest piece, then wafer-level AI), with silicon photonics 'a chunk', hard disk drive a little bigger than GaN, and silicon carbide the least.
quarterly_data.figure: 2H FY26 revenue between $25 million and $30 million; 2H bookings between $60 million and $80 million; non-GAAP EPS between negative $0.09 and negative $0.05

quarterly_data.signal: Package-level burn-in: in the last month Aehr received 'a very large forecast' from its lead Sonoma production customer (an AI ASIC hyperscaler, not named) for AI ASIC production capacity. There is no purchase order yet, but requested shipments of Sonoma production systems and BIMs begin in fiscal Q1 '27 (starting May 30), which management expects to drive 'very strong and potentially record bookings' this fiscal year and significant revenue growth next fiscal year. The customer plans much higher power ASICs later this year; Aehr is developing the HTOL qualification burn-in modules and sockets for Sonoma at a premier Silicon Valley test services company, and that ASIC is forecast to go to production burn-in at OSATs in Asia. Aehr is qualifying the customer's next production device (hoped to run on Sonoma), and for a third device the customer has said it may consider FOX wafer-level burn-in.
quarterly_data.figure: requested Sonoma shipments beginning in the fiscal first quarter of '27

quarterly_data.signal: Sonoma momentum: Aehr announced more than $5.5 million of Sonoma ultra-high-power packaged-part burn-in orders from multiple customers in fiscal Q3 to date, already above total Sonoma orders for all of Q2, including initial orders from a premier Silicon Valley test lab (not named) for the newly introduced higher-power Sonoma that can support full automation, repeat AI orders from existing Sonoma customers, and burn-in modules for a new design 'expected to be high runner'. During Q2 Aehr completed development of a next-generation fully automated higher-power Sonoma supporting up to 2,000 watts per device (devices to be tested this spring are 'almost 2,000 watts per device'), with an optional bolt-on automated handler, and won key new device wins for HTOL qualification that should add test-house capacity, with at least one customer moving to production in late calendar '26.
quarterly_data.figure: more than $5.5 million Sonoma orders in fiscal third quarter to date; up to 2,000 watts per device

quarterly_data.signal: AI wafer-level burn-in: the lead AI wafer-level burn-in customer (not named) is developing its next-generation processor, is discussing additional capacity and forecasts additional system and WaferPak capacity orders this fiscal year, and plans to move to Aehr's fully integrated automated WaferPak aligner for 300-millimeter wafers. For the benchmark with a top-tier AI processor supplier (not named), Aehr completed new fine-pitch WaferPaks for high-current AI processors, now in test on the customer's processors, and expects to complete data collection this quarter; the CEO attributed the slip to package-level test inputs that did not fully apply at wafer level and sized it as 'measured in weeks or a couple of months'.

Two additional AI processor companies have planned wafer-level benchmark evaluations since the prior call (benchmarks typically take about 6 months), both evaluating wafer-level test and burn-in as an alternative to packaged-part or system-level test for large advanced AI modules that combine multiple AI accelerators and stacked high-bandwidth memory; burning in at wafer level avoids scrapping expensive substrates and memory stacks, and management cites estimates that the substrate costs more than a single processor and the HBM even more. The CEO says roadmaps are moving to packages with HBM, high-bandwidth flash and 2, 4 or 8 compute chips, making wafer-level burn-in progressively more valuable, and expects some cannibalization of package-level burn-in ('I think the world is going to be both for a long time').
quarterly_data.figure: 2 additional AI processor companies planning benchmarks; benchmarks typically take about 6 months

quarterly_data.signal: Market sizing and capacity: at wafer level a single processor for the largest customers needs '20, 30 systems or so' of '$4 million, $5 million' machines, with ASPs higher than at package level; the CEO puts today's AI spend on test and burn-in at '$8 billion, $10 billion to maybe $15 billion or so' and says the AI business can be 'measured in hundreds of millions of dollars for Aehr Test a few years out'. He calls Sonoma a highly preferred HTOL system with the largest installed base in test houses worldwide, and says it fills a production burn-in gap: customers had been using system-level or rack test, and existing burn-in 'ovens' were 'maybe 600 watts and below'. Aehr could ship 20 systems a month of each (package and wafer level) during this calendar year, 'bigger than our forecast by a lot'. Demand for the lower-power Echo and Tahoe systems is also rising, from an installed base of more than 100 systems across over 20 semiconductor companies.
quarterly_data.figure: 20, 30 systems or so per processor at $4 million, $5 million each; AI test and burn-in spend $8 billion, $10 billion to maybe $15 billion; capacity 20 systems a month of each

quarterly_data.signal: Flash memory: Aehr completed its wafer-level benchmark with 'a global leader in NAND flash' (not named) just before the holidays, showing higher parallelism and power than traditional probers and group probers; the customer took the wafers back to validate correlation, with feedback expected in the next couple of months. Aehr proposed a next-generation FOX-XP, WaferPak and auto-aligner solution for High Bandwidth Flash (HBF), supporting single-touchdown high-power test on 300-millimeter wafers; development would take over a year after customer commitment. The CEO says the customer shifted focus from enterprise flash to HBF, which 'broke their infrastructure' (power supplies, I/O pins, parallelism), and Aehr expects to increase R&D spend on AI wafer-level burn-in and on the memory system, which will be a blade in the FOX system.
quarterly_data.figure: development over a year following customer commitment

quarterly_data.signal: Other end markets: in GaN, unanticipated high-voltage fault conditions at the lead production customer required WaferPak and protection-circuit redesigns, delaying approximately $2 million in WaferPak shipments from the just-ended quarter into the current one; shipments have resumed, and Aehr is developing WaferPaks for several new GaN device designs headed to high-volume production for data center infrastructure and power delivery, automotive power distribution and electrical breakers. In silicon carbide, the lead customer moved from 150-millimeter to 200-millimeter wafers, nearly doubling output without new FOX-XP systems; it needs more WaferPaks this year, but additional system capacity 'appears to be a year out', so Aehr pushed expected orders to next fiscal year. In hard disk drives, Aehr is installing additional FOX-CP systems for 'a major supplier of hard disk drives' (not named) for wafer-level burn-in of special drive components, with more purchases planned later this calendar year, though the revenue opportunity remains modest.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately $2 million in WaferPak shipments delayed

players.product: burn-in and reliability screening for optical devices — data-center transceivers, chip-to-chip I/O and silicon photonics (FOX wafer-level and Sonoma package-level)

quarterly_data.signal: Silicon photonics: management believes silicon photonics used in data center and chip-to-chip I/O 'is going to be a significant market' driving production burn-in capacity for FOX wafer-level burn-in systems and WaferPaks. The lead silicon photonics customer (not named) 'has now firmed up its production ramp', expected to begin early next fiscal year (fiscal '27); the timing is later than previously expected but aligns with recently announced AI processor platforms, positioning Aehr for calendar 2026 orders and deliveries in fiscal '27. Production systems for this customer are part of the second-half bookings outlook.
quarterly_data.figure: ramp expected early next fiscal year; calendar 2026 orders and deliveries in fiscal '27

quarterly_data.signal: Aehr finalized a forecast with another major silicon photonics customer (not named), initially targeting data center applications with a road map toward optical I/O, and expected to book its initial turnkey FOX system soon, with delivery planned for May; in Q&A, discussing silicon photonics, the CEO said a new customer 'wants a system' by May and Aehr already has a system on its floor, awaiting that customer's purchase order.
quarterly_data.figure: initial turnkey FOX system; delivery planned for May
